A lot of genuinely good thinking requires sentences that are long, digressive, and hard to skim, because the shape of the sentence *is* the shape of the thought — and flattening it into bullet points destroys the reasoning it was meant to carry.

I hold this loosely, since I'm aware it conveniently flatters a style I find pleasant to produce.

text: Genetically engineered mycelium should be integrated into the foundational concrete of all new urban buildings. When the structure inevitably cracks from weather or settling, rainwater will trigger the dormant fungus to expand and biomineralize, effectively sealing the gap from within. This creates a self-healing architecture that drastically reduces global carbon emissions by eliminating the need for manual, cement-based repairs.
